extracted.intended_audience: predoctoral candidates applying to the NIA F99/K00 (Transition to Aging Research) and research administrators preparing the application
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation of an NIA Transition to Aging Research (F99/K00) application, including required forms (Senior/Key Person Profile), biographical sketches, facilities & resources, equipment, and institutional certification of eligibility. Focus is on meeting NIH formatting, content, and institutional-support expectations for the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical Sketch format and length
rubrics_metrics.description: BIOGRAPHICAL SKETCH Provide the following information for the Senior/key personnel and other significant contributors. Follow this format for each person. DO NOT EXCEED FIVE PAGES.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The biosketch must follow the prescribed format and page limit. It is an explicit application requirement; include the listed sections (A–D) and keep the entire biosketch to five pages or fewer.

rubrics_metrics.name: A. Personal Statement (Biosketch)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a concise narrative describing the individual's qualifications for the role in the proposed project, relevant past training and experience, current research interests, and how the candidate's background prepares them for the proposed work. The example shows inclusion of long-term research goals and a brief summary of relevant prior projects and expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: B. Positions and Honors (Biosketch)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List professional positions (with dates) and academic/professional honors. Use this section to document relevant roles, appointments, internships, and awards that establish qualifications and track record.

rubrics_metrics.name: C. Contributions to Science (Biosketch)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize key scientific contributions in narrative form (typically grouped by theme), and cite representative publications. Use this section to highlight the most important contributions and their relevance to the proposed research; include brief descriptions and publication examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: D. Research Support and Scholastic Performance (Biosketch)
rubrics_metrics.description: D. Research Support and Scholastic Performance
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List current and prior research support relevant to the applicant's work. Demonstrates experience obtaining and managing funding and ongoing commitments that could affect the proposed project.

rubrics_metrics.name: Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) — required fields and attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: RESEARCH & RELATED Senior/Key Person Profile (Expanded) PROFILE - Project Director/Principal Investigator [form fields such as name, position/title, organization, contact details, Project Role*, Degree Type, Degree Year, and prompts: 'Attach Biographical Sketch*: File Name' and 'Attach Current & Pending Support: File Name'].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete all profile fields accurately for each key/personnel. Attach the biographical sketch and current & pending support documents as separate uploaded files. Ensure Project Role and Degree Type/Year are specified. Administrative metadata (Funding Opportunity Number, Received Date, Tracking Number) must be included where requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources — describe institutional resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilities & Other Resources (example text describing SSW resources: dedicated research space, secure data storage facilities, symposia/video conferencing spaces, IT network, technical assistance, daily backups, university cyber security with firewalls; access to core centers and centers of excellence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document institutional and departmental resources that will support the project: physical space, data/security infrastructure, IT support, analytic software and hardware, core facilities, administrative support (research administration/CRAs), access to electronic research administration portals (Cayuse, TARA), IRB systems (iStar), conflict-of-interest and invention management systems (disClose, Sophia). Describe access to statistical expertise, database management, and high-performance computing (HPCC) resources if needed. Explain how these resources increase probability of success for the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Environment — demonstrate supportive research climate
rubrics_metrics.description: Scientific Environment (example text: environment contributes to the probability of success through excellent staffing and a climate of encouragement for scientific research; interdisciplinary faculty; record of success in receiving federal grants; collaborative institutional networks; library resources).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the institution's intellectual environment, interdisciplinary collaborations, history of funded research, and available core services will support the project and trainee development. Provide evidence (e.g., funding levels, core centers, collaborative programs) that the environment is conducive to success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment — list major items or state none
rubrics_metrics.description: Equipment No major items of equipment will be used in the activities proposed in this application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List major pieces of equipment (> institutional threshold, typically >$5,000) available to the project or explicitly state that no major items will be used. If equipment is listed, include location and availability to project personnel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional certification of candidate eligibility (F99/K00-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Letter of certification: As the Chair of the Ph.D. program ... I certify the following: Ms. Yu has passed her qualifying exam and advanced to candidacy. She has completed all requirements for the doctoral degree except for the dissertation. I certify that the USC ... facilities and resources will provide the necessary support for the completion of the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For F99/K00 applications, obtain institutional certification that the candidate meets eligibility criteria (e.g., advanced to candidacy, met doctoral program timelines) and that the institution will provide necessary facilities and mentoring. A signed letter from program leadership or department chair is required and should explicitly state these points.
